prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Alder Creek Electrical Distribution Substation supplies approved bays/circuits. Bay Automation Controller (Juniper) sends Bay Status Digest to Station Supervisory Control System (Glasswing); validates requests against mode/interlocks/authority/availability, issues outputs, checks returned indications, flags incomplete/contradictory outcomes, associates inspection tag/equipment/authorized record, degrades aged points. Malformed/stale/unauthorized requests rejected/context-logged. Breaker Control Unit executes accepted commands, returns position/circuit-health; local authority prevails. North Bay Controller/South Bay Controller have non-substitutable authority/confirmation, coordinate shared equipment; North blocks unready-interlock closing, maintains approved local control during communications loss; South reports mode/availability. Glasswing presents authorized controls, quality/staleness; produces Alarm Acknowledgement Slip, retains cleared events, separates current/archival evidence; local indications prevail. Station Gateway carries authorized traffic/indications via configured mappings/access/quality/timestamps; produces Protocol Retry Summary, reports links/errors without changing equipment state; verify post-outage currency. Supervisory/execution/protection layers cannot substitute. Maintenance Remote Terminal: authorized sessions only, no authority/interlock bypass. Feeder Protection Relay (Tandem) independently evaluates/trips using approved settings, produces Relay Diagnostic Note. North Protection Panel houses feeder protection/zone logic, independent trip paths. Transformer Protection Panel independently protects transformer, reports abnormal protection/local operation. Satellite Time Receiver (Bluefin) supplies quality-checked time/Clock Drift Snapshot to Sequence Event Archive (Orchard); holdover/mark loss, not measurement/protection validation. Orchard retains ordered changes/outcomes/source/time/quality/uncertainty/corrections/configuration; audit access/retention/release, protect backups/test recovery. Station DC System powers/monitors control/protection, flags loss; retains Battery Load Test Record. Engineering Workstation: authorized revision-controlled review, no routine commands; Settings Review Receipt; preserve export quality/timestamps, distinguish derivations. Protection Relay Engineer (Larkspur): event/coordination review; revisions require studies/independent approval/window/comparison/testing; discrepancies block release. Substation Supervisor oversees/escalates/exceptions. Switching Desk Coordinator (Keystone): clearances/plan, Isolation Boundary Card, confirmed handback. Control Room Operator uses approved procedures/interface, reviews/acknowledges, logs actions, verifies post-handback consistency; clearance≠correction; unresolved: Clearance Handoff Memo. Substation Field Crew

New part:
S195: Substation Supervisor ensures communication changes, point mapping changes, and control logic changes are managed through station change control.
S196: Substation Field Crew verifies equipment indications locally when remote status is uncertain and reports discrepancies through established operating channels.
S197: Maintenance windows are planned around feeder loading, switching constraints, and the availability of qualified personnel.
S198: The Substation Supervisor coordinates work timing with the Switching Desk Coordinator and confirms that operating responsibilities are understood.
S199: The Control Room Operator reviews the equipment affected by each work package and identifies any required operating restrictions.
S200: The Switching Desk Coordinator confirms switching prerequisites before field work begins and keeps the approved switching sequence current.
S201: Substation Field Crew performs work only after required clearances, isolation, and grounding have been confirmed through established procedures.
S202: Work boundaries are verified locally before personnel approach exposed conductors or operate equipment under maintenance.
S203: The Protection Relay Engineer reviews test scope, approved settings, and restoration criteria before protection testing starts.
S204: Testing is performed with approved procedures, calibrated instruments, and a defined means of stopping the test if unexpected indications occur.
S205: The Engineering Workstation is used for authorized configuration review, and changes are applied only through station change control.
S206: The Maintenance Remote Terminal uses the review receipt to support controlled maintenance review.
S207: The Bay Automation Controller uses the load test record to support maintenance review.
S208: The Station Supervisory Control System receives the Protocol Retry Summary for operational review.
S209: Cinder verifies that field work remains within the approved work boundary and reports any unsafe condition through established channels.
S210: Orchard retains event information needed to review testing and restoration activity.
S211: Feeder Protection Relay testing is coordinated so that protection coverage is not unintentionally removed from an energized feeder.
S212: A protection function placed out of service is tracked by the responsible operator until it is restored and verified.
S213: The Breaker Control Unit is tested using controlled commands that cannot bypass local interlocks or approved operating authority.
S214: Remote commands are inhibited when equipment status is uncertain or when required permissives are unavailable.
S215: If communications are degraded, the Control Room Operator treats remote indications as unavailable until their reliability is established.
S216: Substation Field Crew verifies equipment indications locally when remote status is uncertain and reports discrepancies through established operating channels.
S217: Manual operation is permitted only under approved procedures and with the required local checks and communication with the Control Room Operator.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
